newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea sentences 110 students over campus unrest.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea sentences 110 students over campus unrest.

text.p: A South Korean court on Tuesday sentenced 51 students to jail terms of between eight months and three years for their roles in violent pro-North Korean campus unrest in August, court officials said.
Another 59 students were handed suspended jail sentences of between one year and 1-1/2 years, meaning they will not have to spend times behind bars if they stay out of trouble.
Thousands of students were rounded up after riot police stormed Seoul's Yonsei University to end a seven-day occupation of two campus teaching blocks.
The students were demanding reunification of North and South Korea on Pyongyang's terms. The two Koreas have been technically at war since their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce.
Presiding judge Min Hyong-ki told the court the protests "benefitted the enemy", state media reported.
South Korean authorities have launched a crackdown on a student activist body, the Hanchongryon, which masterminded the Yonsei protests, and on Monday arrested its leader Park Byoung-un, 23.
